# Introduction

This workflow has been created to map bird data from the [National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON)](https://www.neonscience.org/) to Darwin Core and the [Humboldt Extension for Ecological Inventories](https://eco.tdwg.org/). The workflow produces four Darwin Core tables: Event, HumboldtEcologicalInventory, Occurrence, and ExtendedMeasurementOrFact.  
The dataset is structured hierarchically, with events defined at multiple levels (project, domain, site, plot, point and point-count survey). Occurrences represent observed birds. Contextual information on sampling design, effort, and scope is expressed through Humboldt Extension terms.

## Introduction to NEON Bird Observations

NEON’s breeding landbird point count dataset provides taxonomic identifications, detection methods, and associated survey and site information for birds observed during standardized six-minute surveys. The protocol focuses on diurnal, terrestrial breeding landbirds, a group chosen because they respond strongly to changes in climate, habitat, and land use.

Field crews survey spatially distributed plots across NEON <a href="https://www.neonscience.org/field-sites" target="_blank">field sites</a> during the breeding season every year, recording every bird seen or heard. These repeated surveys produce rich detection–nondetection data suited for occupancy modeling.

NEON’s terrestrial field **sites** are designated as *large* or *small*, which determines the sampling design. Large sites are surveyed once per year and contain 5–10 **plots** each containing a bird grid, made up of a 3×3 array of nine **points** spaced 250 m apart (see Figure 1). Field crews visit every point in a grid and conduct a 6-minute **point-count survey**. Smaller sites, which cannot accommodate full grids, contain 2–25 point-count locations randomly distributed across the site and spaced at least 250 m apart. These are surveyed twice per year.

<div id="ds-dataTip" markdown="1">
<i class="fa fa-star"></i> **Data Tip:** NEON’s bird data follow a hierarchical structure: DomainID → SiteID → PlotID → PointID. Large sites use points labeled 1–9, while small sites use point label 21 for all locations.
For example: (Large Site) D07 → GRSM → GRSM_002 → 5 | (Small Site) D20 → PUUM → PUUM_001 → 21.
</div> 

<figure>
	<a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anushkakg/Bird-Occupancy-Modeling/refs/heads/main/images/birdGrid.jpg">
	<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anushkakg/Bird-Occupancy-Modeling/refs/heads/main/images/birdGrid.jpg" alt="Design of the bird point count grid, consisting of 9 points separated by a minimum of 250 m."></a>

	</figcaption>
</figure>

More details on NEON’s bird monitoring program are available on the <a href="https://www.neonscience.org/data-collection/birds" target="_blank">NEON bird resource page</a>. Protocols referenced in the data can be found in the <a href="https://data.neonscience.org/documents" target="_blank">Document Library</a>.

# Load libraries

The code examples in this document use R functions provided by the `neonUtilities` package together with `dplyr` for data manipulation. These libraries allow automated download and processing of NEON data products to prepare them for mapping to Darwin Core and the Humboldt Extension.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(neonUtilities)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
```

# Download Data

The data used in this example come from one NEON data products: Breeding landbird point counts. This workflow uses data from **[RELEASE-2026](https://www.neonscience.org/data-samples/data-management/data-revisions-releases/RELEASE-2026)**.  

- [NEON 2026] NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network) [1]. 2026. Breeding landbird point counts (DP1.10003.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/v6hs-mx57. Dataset accessed from [NEON Data Portal](https://data.neonscience.org/data-products/DP1.10003.001/RELEASE-2026) on 2026-09-14.  

A NEON token was used to download the original data for this workflow. Tokens are optional but recommended, as they allow authenticated access and help avoid API rate limits when downloading large datasets. Users preparing their own mappings may wish to generate a personal token. For more information, see the [Using an API Token when Accessing NEON Data with neonUtilities tutorial](https://www.neonscience.org/resources/learning-hub/tutorials/neon-api-tokens-tutorial) and the [NEON API token documentation](https://data.neonscience.org/data-api/rate-limiting/#api-tokens).

## Get Bird data

```{r}
if (!dir.exists("data")) {
  dir.create("data")
}

if (!dir.exists("outputs")) {
  dir.create("outputs")
}

if (!dir.exists("outputs/full")) {
  dir.create("outputs/full")
}

if (!dir.exists("outputs/zipped")) {
  dir.create("outputs/zipped")
}

if (file.exists("data/bird.occurrence.RData")) {
  load("data/bird.occurrence.RData")
} else {
  
  bird.occurrence <- loadByProduct(dpID="DP1.10003.001", 
                                   package = "expanded",
                                   release = "RELEASE-2026",
                                   token = Sys.getenv("NEON_TOKEN"),
                                   check.size = F)
  
  save(bird.occurrence, file = "data/bird.occurrence.RData")
}

```
# Map Data

NEON provides separate tables for point-count survey metadata (`brd_perpoint`) and the bird counts themselves (`brd_countdata`).

`brd_perpoint` contains fields describing the location, elevation, date and field-crew recorded weather conditions for each point-count survey. 

```{r brd_perpoint}
str(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint)

head(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint, n=5)
```

`brd_countdata` contains data for the birds observed during each point-count survey, including identification, observation method, distance, and observed minute.

```{r brd_countdata}
str(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata)

head(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata, n=5)
```

## Preparing the Data

### Create unique IDs

Each point-count survey needs a unique identifier so that we can match each point-count survey record (brd_perpoint) to its corresponding bird data (brd_countdata). We extract the survey year from eventID and then combine the site, plot, point, year, and bout into a single key called pointSurveyID for each of the tables. Note, because the siteID is already included in the plotID (e.g., BART_012), siteID is not actually included in the construction of `pointSurveyID`.

```{r}
#add pointLocationIDs
bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint <- bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint %>%
  mutate(year = str_extract(eventID, "\\d{4}")) %>%
  mutate(pointLocationID = paste(plotID, "point", pointID, sep = "_"))

bird.occurrence$brd_countdata <- bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
  mutate(year = str_extract(eventID, "\\d{4}")) %>%
  mutate(pointLocationID = paste(plotID, "point", pointID, sep = "_"))

#add pointSurveyIDs
bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint <- bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint %>%
  mutate(year = str_extract(eventID, "\\d{4}")) %>%
  mutate(pointSurveyID = paste(plotID, "point", pointID, year, "bout", boutNumber, sep = "_"))

bird.occurrence$brd_countdata <- bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
  mutate(year = str_extract(eventID, "\\d{4}")) %>%
  mutate(pointSurveyID = paste(plotID, "point", pointID, year, "bout", boutNumber, sep = "_"))
```

### Create date column

```{r}
bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate <- as.Date(
  bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$startDate
)

bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$eventDate <- as.Date(
  bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$startDate
)
```


## Map Event Core & Humboldt Data

The event hierarchy presented here follows the structure of NEON’s sampling design, with events defined at project, domain, site, plot, point, and individual sampling event (point-count survey) levels. Some event-level information is not provided directly in the NEON data download, such as details describing the overall project, individual domains, and sites. To capture the full hierarchy of the sampling design, these additional levels are reconstructed and included in the event table. The values are hard-coded based on latest (2025-09-24) NEON information.  

Domain-level metadata was compiled from NEON documentation and geospatial files. A polygon shapefile defining NEON’s domain boundaries was downloaded from [NEONDomains_2024.zip](https://www.neonscience.org/sites/default/files/NEONDomains_2024.zip) (last updated October 2024, CRS: Geographic WGS 84). Domain centroids (latitude and longitude) and associated uncertainty values were calculated from this shapefile using ArcGIS.  

Site-level metadata was retrieved directly from NEON’s public API on September 24, 2025 using the field site metadata download (*NEON_Field_Site_Metadata_20250924*). This download represents a flattened subset of the full JSON objects returned by the [locations/sites API endpoint](https://data.neonscience.org/api/v0/locations/sites).

All fields from the [survey event table template](https://github.com/gbif/doc-guide-publishing-survey-data/tree/1.1_postCommReview/data/event_template_wHE_event-table.csv) are retained for completeness, even when particular values are not applicable for this dataset.  

### Project Event

The project event describes the overall bird monitoring program within NEON. It defines the scope of the survey (taxonomic, geographic, temporal), the general sampling protocols, and whether absence, abundance, and material samples are reported. The data for the Event Core and Humboldt extension are split into two separate files.

Mapping Event core fields for the project event level:

```{r}
NEON_project_event_core <- data.frame(eventID = "NEON",
                                      parentEventID = NA,
                                      fieldNumber = NA,
                                      habitat = NA,
                                      locationID = NA,
                                      countryCode = "US",
                                      decimalLatitude = NA,
                                      decimalLongitude = NA,
                                      coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = NA,
                                      geodeticDatum = NA,
                                      locality = NA,
                                      sampleSizeValue = NA,
                                      sampleSizeUnit = NA,
                                      footprintWKT = NA,
                                      footprintSRS = NA,
                                      eventDate = paste(
                                        min(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate, na.rm = TRUE),
                                        max(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate, na.rm = TRUE),
                                        sep = "/"
                                      ),
                                      eventTime = NA,
                                      eventType = "project",
                                      samplingProtocol = "Point-count Survey",
                                      dataGeneralizations = NA,
                                      informationWithheld = NA,
                                      fieldNotes = NA,
                                      eventRemarks = NA,
                                      identifiedBy = NA
                                    )
```

### Domain Events

Domains represent NEON’s ecoclimatic regions. Each domain includes one or more terrestrial sites where bird sampling occurs.

Setup:

```{r}
NEON_domain_metadata <- read.csv("data/NEON_Domain_Metadata_20250924.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

NEON_domain_list <- unique(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint[, c("domainID")])

#index
domain_idx <- match(NEON_domain_list, NEON_domain_metadata$domain_id)
```

Mapping Event core fields for the domain event level:

```{r}
added_domain_data_core <- data.frame(eventID = NEON_domain_metadata$domain_id[domain_idx],
                                      parentEventID = "NEON",
                                      fieldNumber = NA,
                                      habitat = NA,
                                      locationID = NEON_domain_metadata$domain_id[domain_idx],
                                      countryCode = "US",
                                      decimalLatitude = NEON_domain_metadata$decimalLatitude[domain_idx],
                                      decimalLongitude = NEON_domain_metadata$decimalLongitude[domain_idx],
                                      coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = NEON_domain_metadata$coordinateUncertaintyinMeters[domain_idx],
                                      geodeticDatum = "WGS84",
                                      locality = paste(NEON_domain_metadata$domain_name[domain_idx], " (", NEON_domain_metadata$domain_id[domain_idx], ")", sep = ""),
                                      sampleSizeValue = NA,
                                      sampleSizeUnit = NA,
                                      footprintWKT = NA,
                                      footprintSRS = NA,
                                      eventDate = tapply(
                                        bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate,
                                        bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$domainID,
                                        function(x) paste(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), sep = "/")
                                      )[NEON_domain_list],
                                      eventTime = NA,
                                      eventType = "survey", #eventType describes the event, not the internal vocabulary
                                      samplingProtocol = "Point-count Survey",
                                      dataGeneralizations = NA,
                                      informationWithheld = NA,
                                      fieldNotes = NA,
                                      eventRemarks = NA,
                                      identifiedBy = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
                                        group_by(domainID) %>%
                                        summarise(
                                          identifiedBy = paste(sort(unique(identifiedBy)), collapse = " | "),
                                          .groups = "drop"
                                        ) %>%
                                        right_join(data.frame(domainID = NEON_domain_list), by = "domainID") %>%
                                        arrange(match(domainID, NEON_domain_list)) %>%
                                        mutate(identifiedBy = ifelse(is.na(identifiedBy), NA, identifiedBy)) %>%
                                        pull(identifiedBy)
                                    )
```

### Site Events

Each NEON terrestrial site contains designated locations for breeding landbird point-count surveys. Large sites contain 5–10 plots, each with a 3×3 grid of nine points spaced 250 m apart, while small sites contain 2–25 randomly distributed point-count locations spaced at least 250 m apart. Site events record location metadata, habitat information, and elevation.

Setup:

```{r}
NEON_site_metadata <- read.csv(
  "https://www.neonscience.org/field-sites/exports/NEON_Field_Site_Metadata_20250924",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

NEON_site_list <- unique(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint[, c("siteID")])

#indexes
site_idx <- match(NEON_site_list, NEON_site_metadata$site_id)
```

Mapping Event core fields for the site event level:

```{r}
added_site_data_core <- data.frame(eventID = NEON_site_metadata$site_id[site_idx],
                                    parentEventID = NEON_site_metadata$domain_id[site_idx],
                                    fieldNumber = NA,
                                    habitat = gsub("\\|", " | ", NEON_site_metadata$dominant_nlcd_classes[site_idx]),
                                    locationID = NEON_site_metadata$site_id[site_idx],
                                    countryCode = "US",
                                    county = NEON_site_metadata$site_county[site_idx],
                                    stateProvince = NEON_site_metadata$site_state[site_idx],
                                    decimalLatitude = NEON_site_metadata$latitude[site_idx],
                                    decimalLongitude = NEON_site_metadata$longitude[site_idx],
                                    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = NA,
                                    geodeticDatum = "WGS84",
                                    locality = paste(NEON_site_metadata$site_name[site_idx], " (", NEON_site_metadata$site_id[site_idx], ")", sep = ""),
                                    minimumElevationInMeters = NEON_site_metadata$minimum_elevation_m[site_idx],
                                    maximumElevationInMeters = NEON_site_metadata$maximum_elevation_m[site_idx],
                                    verbatimElevation = paste(NEON_site_metadata$mean_evelation_m[site_idx], "m", sep=""),
                                    sampleSizeValue = NA,
                                    sampleSizeUnit = NA,
                                    footprintWKT = NA,
                                    footprintSRS = NA,
                                    eventDate = tapply(
                                      bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate,
                                      bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$siteID,
                                      function(x) paste(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), sep = "/")
                                    )[NEON_site_list],
                                    eventTime = NA,
                                    eventType = "survey",
                                    samplingProtocol = "Point-count Survey",
                                    dataGeneralizations = NA,
                                    informationWithheld = NA,
                                    fieldNotes = NA,
                                    eventRemarks = NA,
                                    identifiedBy = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
                                      group_by(siteID) %>%
                                      summarise(
                                        identifiedBy = paste(sort(unique(identifiedBy)), collapse = " | "),
                                        .groups = "drop"
                                      ) %>%
                                      right_join(data.frame(siteID = NEON_site_list), by = "siteID") %>%
                                      arrange(match(siteID, NEON_site_list)) %>%
                                      mutate(identifiedBy = ifelse(is.na(identifiedBy), NA, identifiedBy)) %>%
                                      pull(identifiedBy)
                                  )
```

```{r}
                                        taxonCompletenessProtocols = "Standardized point-count surveys are designed to detect all diurnal terrestrial breeding landbird species seen or heard during the survey period.",
                                        hasNonTargetTaxa = "false",
                                        areNonTargetTaxaFullyReported = NA,
                                        nonTargetTaxa = NA,
                                        targetLifeStageScope = "adult | juvenile",
                                        excludedLifeStageScope = "egg | nestling",
                                        isLifeStageScopeFullyReported = "true",
                                        targetDegreeOfEstablishmentScope = NA,
                                        excludedDegreeOfEstablishmentScope = NA,
                                        isDegreeOfEstablishmentScopeFullyReported = NA,
                                        targetGrowthFormScope = NA,
                                        excludedGrowthFormScope = NA,
                                        isGrowthFormScopeFullyReported = NA,
                                        hasNonTargetOrganisms = NA,
                                        targetHabitatScope = NA,
                                        excludedHabitatScope = NA,
                                        samplingEffort = "6-minute point count per survey location",
                                        isSamplingEffortReported = "true",
                                        samplingEffortProtocol = "Birds are surveyed using standardized 6-minute point counts at each sampling location. Field crews record all birds seen or heard during the survey. Large sites contain 5–10 plots with nine points per grid and are surveyed once annually, while small sites contain 2–25 point-count locations and are surveyed twice annually.",
                                        samplingEffortValue = "6",
                                        samplingEffortUnit = "minutes per point-count survey",
                                        samplingPerformedBy = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint %>%
                                          group_by(siteID) %>%
                                          summarise(
                                            samplingPerformedBy = paste(
                                              sort(unique(measuredBy[!is.na(measuredBy)])),
                                              collapse = " | "
                                            ),
                                            .groups = "drop"
                                          ) %>%
                                          right_join(data.frame(siteID = NEON_site_list), by = "siteID") %>%
                                          arrange(match(siteID, NEON_site_list)) %>%
                                          mutate(
                                            samplingPerformedBy = ifelse(
                                              samplingPerformedBy == "",
                                              NA,
                                              samplingPerformedBy
                                            )
                                          ) %>%
                                          pull(samplingPerformedBy)
                                      )
```


### Plot Events

Plot events represent spatial sampling units within NEON’s breeding landbird monitoring design. At large sites, each plot contains a 3×3 grid of nine point-count locations spaced 250 m apart. At small sites, plots contain a single point-count location. Plot-level metadata include plot identifiers, habitat information, and elevation.

Setup:

```{r}
NEON_plot_metadata <- unique(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint[, c("namedLocation",
                                                               "siteID",
                                                               "plotID",
                                                               "plotType",
                                                               "nlcdClass",
                                                               "decimalLatitude",
                                                               "decimalLongitude",
                                                               "geodeticDatum",
                                                               "coordinateUncertainty",
                                                               "elevation",
                                                               "elevationUncertainty")])
```

Mapping Event core fields for the plot event level:

```{r}
added_plot_data_core <- data.frame(eventID = NEON_plot_metadata$plotID,
                                    parentEventID = NEON_plot_metadata$siteID,
                                    fieldNumber = NA,
                                    habitat = NEON_plot_metadata$nlcdClass,
                                    locationID = NEON_plot_metadata$plotID,
                                    countryCode = "US",
                                    decimalLatitude = NEON_plot_metadata$decimalLatitude,
                                    decimalLongitude = NEON_plot_metadata$decimalLongitude,
                                    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = NEON_plot_metadata$coordinateUncertainty,
                                    geodeticDatum = "WGS84",
                                    locality = NEON_plot_metadata$plotID,
                                    minimumElevationInMeters = NEON_plot_metadata$elevation - NEON_plot_metadata$elevationUncertainty,
                                    maximumElevationInMeters = NEON_plot_metadata$elevation + NEON_plot_metadata$elevationUncertainty,
                                    verbatimElevation = paste(NEON_plot_metadata$elevation, "m", sep=""),
                                    sampleSizeValue = NA,
                                    sampleSizeUnit = NA,
                                    footprintWKT = NA,
                                    footprintSRS = NA,
                                    eventDate = tapply(
                                      bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate,
                                      bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$plotID,
                                      function(x) paste(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), sep = "/")
                                    )[NEON_plot_metadata$plotID],
                                    eventTime = NA,
                                    eventType = "survey",
                                    samplingProtocol = "Point-count Survey",
                                    dataGeneralizations = NA,
                                    informationWithheld = NA,
                                    fieldNotes = NA,
                                    eventRemarks = NA,

                                      bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$plotID,
                                      function(x) paste(sort(unique(x)), collapse = " | ")
                                    )[NEON_plot_metadata$plotID]
                                  )
```

### Point Events

Point events represent the smallest sampling units within NEON’s breeding landbird monitoring design. At large sites, each plot contains a 3×3 grid of nine point-count locations spaced 250 m apart. At small sites, plots contain a single point-count location.

Setup:

```{r}
NEON_point_metadata <- bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint %>%
  group_by(pointLocationID) %>%
  summarise(
    plotID = first(plotID),
    observedHabitat = paste(
      sort(unique(observedHabitat[!is.na(observedHabitat)])),
      collapse = " | "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Point Visit Events

Point-count visit events describe individual breeding landbird surveys conducted at a designated point. At this level, we record the survey date and time, observer, detection conditions, and other field information. During each standardized six-minute survey, all birds seen or heard are recorded, including detections used to determine presence or nondetection. These events link the hierarchical survey design to the occurrence records derived from individual bird observations.

Mapping Event core fields for the point visit event level:

```{r}
added_point_visit_data_core <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$pointSurveyID,
                                          parentEventID = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$pointLocationID,
                                          fieldNumber = NA,
                                          habitat = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$observedHabitat,
                                          locationID = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$pointLocationID,
                                          countryCode = "US",
                                          decimalLatitude = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$decimalLatitude,
                                          decimalLongitude = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$decimalLongitude,
                                          coordinateUncertaintyInMeters = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$coordinateUncertainty,
                                          geodeticDatum = "WGS84",
                                          locality = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$pointLocationID,
                                          minimumElevationInMeters = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$elevation - bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$elevationUncertainty,
                                          maximumElevationInMeters = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$elevation + bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$elevationUncertainty,
                                          verbatimElevation = paste(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$elevation, "m", sep=""),
                                          sampleSizeValue = NA,
                                          sampleSizeUnit = NA,
                                          footprintWKT = NA,
                                          footprintSRS = NA,
                                          eventDate = paste(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$eventDate),
                                          eventTime = ifelse(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$samplingImpractical == "OK",
                                            paste0(
                                              format(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$startDate, "%H:%M:%S"),
                                              "/",
                                              format(
                                                bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$startDate + lubridate::minutes(6),
                                                "%H:%M:%S"
                                              )
                                            ),
                                            format(bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$startDate, "%H:%M:%S")
                                          ),
                                          eventType = "site visit",
                                          samplingProtocol = "Point-count Survey",
                                          dataGeneralizations = NA,
                                          informationWithheld = NA,
                                          fieldNotes = NA,
                                          eventRemarks = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint$remarks,
                                          identifiedBy = bird.occurrence$brd_perpoint %>% 
                                            left_join(
                                              bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
                                                group_by(pointSurveyID) %>%
                                                summarise(
                                                  identifiedBy = paste(sort(unique(identifiedBy)), collapse = " | "),
                                                  .groups = "drop"
                                                ),
                                              by = "pointSurveyID"
                                            ) %>%
                                            pull(identifiedBy)
                                        )
```

### Merge Event Tables

```{r}
event_data_core <- bind_rows(
  NEON_project_event_core,
  added_domain_data_core,
  added_site_data_core,
  added_plot_data_core,
  added_point_data_core,
  added_point_visit_data_core
)

event_data_humboldt <- bind_rows(
  NEON_project_event_humboldt,
  added_domain_data_humboldt,
  added_site_data_humboldt,
  added_plot_data_humboldt,
  added_point_data_humboldt,
  added_point_visit_data_humboldt
)

rownames(event_data_core) <- NULL
event_data_core <- event_data_core %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) #Remove columns that are entirely NA

rownames(event_data_humboldt) <- NULL
event_data_humboldt <- event_data_humboldt %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) #Remove columns that are entirely NA
```

## Map Occurrence Data

Occurrence data represent the biological entities observed or derived within events. 

- Birds observed in the field are represented as observed records identified to species, sex or age where possible. These records only report presences. Absences of birds are instead recorded at the plot visit event level, where a complete lack of observations indicates that no birds were found during sampling.  

### Bird Occurrences

```{r}
added_bird_occurrence_data <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointSurveyID,
                                         occurrenceID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$uid,
                                         basisOfRecord = "HumanObservation",
                                         catalogNumber = NA,
                                         scientificName = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$scientificName,
                                         scientificNameAuthorship = NA,
                                         taxonRank = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$taxonRank,
                                         taxonID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$taxonID,
                                         kingdom = "Animalia",
                                         identificationQualifier = NA,
                                         identificationReferences = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
                                           left_join(bird.occurrence$brd_references %>%
                                                       select(date, siteID, identificationReferences),
                                                     by = c("eventDate" = "date", "siteID")) %>%
                                           pull(identificationReferences),
                                         identificationRemarks = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata %>%
                                           left_join(bird.occurrence$brd_identificationHistory %>%
                                                       select(identificationHistoryID, remarks, previousTaxonID = taxonID, acceptedTaxonID),
                                                     by = "identificationHistoryID") %>%
                                           mutate(identificationRemarks = ifelse(is.na(identificationHistoryID), NA_character_,
                                             paste0(remarks, "; previous taxonID: ", previousTaxonID, "; accepted taxonID: ", acceptedTaxonID))) %>%
                                           pull(identificationRemarks),
                                         eventDate = paste(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$eventDate),
                                         eventTime = format(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$startDate +
                                              lubridate::minutes(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointCountMinute - 1),
                                            "%H:%M:%S"
                                         ),
                                         occurrenceStatus = ifelse(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$targetTaxaPresent == "Y",
                                            "present",
                                            "absent"
                                         ),
                                         organismQuantity = NA, #individualCount is used instead
                                         organismQuantityType = NA, #individualCount is used instead
                                         individualCount = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$clusterSize,
                                         recordedByID = NA, #This information is in the plot visit event
                                         vernacularName = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$vernacularName,
                                         sex = ifelse(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$sexOrAge %in% c("Male", "Female"),
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$sexOrAge,
                                            NA_character_
                                         ),
                                         lifeStage = ifelse(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$sexOrAge == "Juvenile",
                                            "Juvenile",
                                            ifelse(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$sexOrAge %in% c("Male", "Female"),
                                                   "Adult", NA_character_)
                                         ),
                                         establishmentMeans = NA,
                                         degreeOfEstablishment = NA,
                                         pathway = NA,
                                         vitality = "alive",
                                         preparations = NA,
                                         institutionID = NA,
                                         identifiedBy = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$identifiedBy,
                                         occurrenceRemarks = ifelse(
                                            bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$targetTaxaPresent == "N",
                                            "No birds detected during this survey minute",
                                            NA_character_
                                         )
                               )

```

### Merge Occurrence Tables

```{r}
occurrence_data <- bind_rows(added_bird_occurrence_data)
rownames(occurrence_data) <- NULL
occurrence_data <- occurrence_data %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) #Remove columns that are entirely NA
```

## Map Extended Measurement or Fact Data

Certain details do not fit into the core event or occurrence tables. These are represented in the ExtendedMeasurementOrFact (eMoF) table.

### Observer Distance

```{r}
emof_obdistance_data <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointSurveyID,
                             occurrenceID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$uid,
                             measurementType = "observerDistance",
                             measurementValue = as.character(bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$observerDistance),
                             measurementUnit = "m",
                             measurementRemarks = "Radial distance between the observer and the individual(s) being observed"
)
```

### Detection Method

```{r}
emof_detect_method_data <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointSurveyID,
                                     occurrenceID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$uid,
                                     measurementType = "detectionMethod",
                                     measurementValue = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$detectionMethod,
                                     measurementRemarks = "How the individual(s) was (were) first detected by the observer"
)
```

### Visual Confirmation

```{r}
emof_confirm_data <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointSurveyID,
                                     occurrenceID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$uid,
                                     measurementType = "visualConfirmation",
                                     measurementValue = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$visualConfirmation,
                                     measurementRemarks = "Whether the individual(s) was (were) seen after the initial detection"
)
```

### Cluster Code

```{r}
emof_code_data <- data.frame(eventID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$pointSurveyID,
                                     occurrenceID = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$uid,
                                     measurementType = "clusterCode",
                                     measurementValue = bird.occurrence$brd_countdata$clusterCode,
                                     measurementRemarks = "Alphabetic code (A-Z) linked to clusters (groups of individuals of the same species) spanning multiple records"
)
```

### Merge Extended Measurement or Fact Tables

```{r}
emof_data <- bind_rows(emof_obdistance_data,
                       emof_detect_method_data,
                       emof_confirm_data,
                       emof_code_data
                       ) %>%
              filter(!is.na(measurementValue) & measurementValue != "")
rownames(emof_data) <- NULL
```

# Save Data

## Full Dataset

The full processed event and occurrence tables generated through this workflow are available in the project repository. [NEONBirdstoHumboldt/outputs/full](https://github.com/sunray1/NEONBirdstoHumboldt/tree/master/outputs/full).

```{r}
write.csv(event_data_core, "outputs/full/event.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(event_data_humboldt, "outputs/full/humboldtecologicalinventory.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(occurrence_data, "outputs/full/occurrence.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(emof_data, "outputs/full/extendedMeasurementOrFact.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

## Zipped DwC-A

We also save the full dataset as a DwC-A for publishing.

Write data files:

```{r}
write.csv(event_data_core, "outputs/zipped/event.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(event_data_humboldt, "outputs/zipped/humboldtecologicalinventory.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(occurrence_data, "outputs/zipped/occurrence.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
write.csv(emof_data, "outputs/zipped/extendedMeasurementOrFact.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

Create meta.xml files (the file describing the structure of the data):

```{r}
# function to create fields
make_fields_xml <- function(df, prefix) {
  paste0(
    '    <field index="', seq_along(colnames(df)) - 1,
    '" term="', paste0(prefix, colnames(df)), '"/>',
    collapse = "\n"
  )
}

# Event Core
core_xml <- paste0(
'<core encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="\\n" 
       fieldsEnclosedBy="&quot;" ignoreHeaderLines="1"
       rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Event">

  <files>
    <location>event.csv</location>
  </files>

  <id index="0"/>\n',
make_fields_xml(event_data_core, "http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/"),
'\n</core>\n'
)

# Humboldt Extension
humboldt_xml <- paste0(
'<extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="\\n" 
           fieldsEnclosedBy="&quot;" ignoreHeaderLines="1"
           rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/eco/terms/Event">

  <files>
    <location>humboldtecologicalinventory.csv</location>
  </files>

  <coreid index="0"/>\n',
make_fields_xml(event_data_humboldt, "http://rs.tdwg.org/eco/terms/"),
'\n</extension>\n'
)

# Occurrence Extension
occ_xml <- paste0(
'<extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="\\n" 
           fieldsEnclosedBy="&quot;" ignoreHeaderLines="1"
           rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Occurrence">

  <files>
    <location>occurrence.csv</location>
  </files>

  <coreid index="0"/>\n',
make_fields_xml(occurrence_data, "http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/"),
'\n</extension>\n'
)

# extendedMeasurementOrFact Extension
emof_xml <- paste0(
'<extension encoding="UTF-8" fieldsTerminatedBy="," linesTerminatedBy="\\n" 
           fieldsEnclosedBy="&quot;" ignoreHeaderLines="1"
           rowType="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/MeasurementOrFact">

  <files>
    <location>extendedMeasurementOrFact.csv</location>
  </files>

  <coreid index="0"/>\n',
make_fields_xml(emof_data, "http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/"),
'\n</extension>\n'
)

# Put everything together
meta_xml <- paste0(
'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<archive xmlns="http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/text/" metadata="eml.xml">

',
core_xml,
humboldt_xml,
occ_xml,
emof_xml,
'</archive>'
)

writeLines(meta_xml, "outputs/zipped/meta.xml")
```

```{r}
        <para>
          The National Science Foundation's National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) is a continental-scale ecological observation facility, fully funded by NSF and operated by Battelle. NEON collects and provides open data from 81 field sites across the United States that characterize and quantify how our nation's ecosystems are changing. Each year, NEON collects and archives over 100,000 specimens and samples that complement the field observations and automated measurements collected at field sites. These samples represent a rich resource unique among natural history collections due to NEON's utility for continental- and decadal-scale ecology. NEON's archival samples are available upon request to support research studies and analyses. The comprehensive data, spatial extent and remote sensing technology provided by the NEON project will contribute to a better understanding and more accurate forecasting of how human activities impact ecology and how our society can more effectively address critical ecological questions and issues.

additional_description_block <- paste0(
'    <purpose>
      <para>
        The purpose of this dataset is to make breeding landbird monitoring data from the National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) available through GBIF. The data have been structured using the Darwin Core standard and the Humboldt Extension for Ecological Inventories to support discovery, reuse, integration, and ecological analysis. Code used to transform the original NEON data into this Darwin Core Archive, including all data processing and mapping steps, is available at 
        <ulink url="https://sunray1.github.io/NEONBirdstoHumboldt/"><citetitle>NEON Birds to Humboldt workflow</citetitle></ulink>.
      </para>
    </purpose>

    <introduction>
      <para>
        The workflow produces four Darwin Core tables: Event, HumboldtEcologicalInventory, Occurrence, and ExtendedMeasurementOrFact. The dataset is structured hierarchically, with events defined at multiple levels (project, domain, site, plot, point, and point visit). Occurrences represent observed birds. Contextual information on sampling design, effort, and scope is expressed through Humboldt Extension terms.
      </para>
    
      <para>
        The U.S. National Science Foundation’s National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON) carries out long-term, standardized monitoring of breeding landbirds across terrestrial sites in the United States. Birds are surveyed during the breeding season using standardized six-minute point counts. Observers record birds seen or heard and collect information including species identification, detection method, distance from the observer, sex and age when possible, and environmental conditions.
      </para>
    
      <para>
        Bird sampling is spatially distributed across NEON terrestrial sites. At most sites, sampling locations are arranged in 3 x 3 grids of nine points spaced 250 m apart. At sites that cannot accommodate these grids, individual points are distributed throughout the site with a minimum spacing of 250 m. Additional details on NEON’s breeding landbird monitoring program are available from the NEON bird resource page 
        (<ulink url="https://www.neonscience.org/data-collection/birds"><citetitle>NEON bird data resource</citetitle></ulink>) 
        and associated protocols in the NEON Document Library 
        (<ulink url="https://data.neonscience.org/documents"><citetitle>NEON Document Library</citetitle></ulink>).
      </para>
    
      <para>
        NEON biological datasets are organized as hierarchical structures that reflect the standardized design of the survey program. Locality information is captured at multiple spatial scales, including domains, sites, plots, and point-count locations. Sampling context is described using the Darwin Core Event Core and Humboldt Extension, while measurements associated with bird observations are recorded using the Extended Measurement or Fact (eMoF) extension. Occurrence records are linked to point-count survey events to represent bird detections and nondetections.
      </para>
    </introduction>

    <gettingStarted>
      <para>
        The dataset is provided as a Darwin Core Archive consisting of an Event Core file and associated extensions, including HumboldtEcologicalInventory, Occurrence, MeasurementOrFact, and a Humboldt Extension table describing ecological inventory context. These components are linked through shared identifiers such as eventID and occurrenceID.
      </para>
    </gettingStarted>\n'
)
```

Zip files to a DwC-A:

```{r}
output_zip <- "outputs/zipped/DwC-A.zip"

if (file.exists(output_zip)) {
  unlink(output_zip)
}

file_paths <- list.files("outputs/zipped", full.names = TRUE)
zip(zipfile = output_zip, files = file_paths, flags = "-j" )

if (file.exists(output_zip)) {
  unlink(file_paths)
}
```
